findings.what: Interior word positions inside a text run drift up to 7.2pt out of alignment because the emitter reproduces a run's total width with one uniform letter-spacing value instead of the source's per-character origins.

findings.evidence: Looked at 8x side-by-side crops of y 183-194pt in two halves (x 105-360 and x 340-600). Both lines start and end at the same x (the second crop shows "...by using BIR Form No. 1905)" landing identically), which is exactly why the geometric differ scores text_pct 100.0. Went to the data: forms/1601c-2018/index.html emits the run as a single div with letter-spacing:0.0668pt applied uniformly (same pattern on the equivalent 1602Q run), while build/ir/<slug>.ir.json records true per-character positions in char_origin_offsets_pt. Computing max|uniform-model - true origin| per run over all six forms: 1601-fq-2020 10/355 runs >0.5pt, 1601c-2018 47/293, 1601eq-2019 3/472, 1602q-2019 64/520, 1603q-2018 41/299, 1604c-2018 3/108. Root cause from the data: build/ir/2550m-undated.ir.json records only {x0,y0,x1,y1} for the image with no transform/CTM field. fitz get_image_info on the source PDFs shows 2550M's placement matrix has d = -36.72 while every other form I reviewed (2200C +28.08, 2200M +28.08, 2316 +31.01, 2550-DS +39.65, 2550Q +29.70) has the opposite sign. findings.resolution: emit.py applies image["transform"], the full 6-element matrix, to a unit-square <image>: `transform="matrix(40.8,0,0,-36.72,30.48,74.64)"`. The flip is not special-cased - the matrix is carried, which also covers 0605's non-zero `b` - and it is applied only when its own box agrees with the extractor's to 0.005pt, so a matrix the two views could not reconcile falls back to the box. findings.what: The guide's ALPHANUMERIC TAX CODE table binds tax rates to the wrong ATC codes. The official page draws six columns (ATC | Percentage Tax On | Tax Rate, twice); the reflow glues the second and fourth and fifth into one cell, so descriptions and rates from the right-hand half migrate onto left-hand codes. findings.what: The ?debug=fields overlay shipped in every forms/ bundle is the OLD self-referential one, not the fixed overlay. The fixed overlay (fits/small/over/unboxed/vacant, with blue meaning 'printed box with NO input') exists only in tools/formgen/emit.py and has never been regenerated into the corpus. In the shipped overlay blue dashed means the opposite - 'this input is fine' - so a reviewer reading the shipped legend reads every verdict backwards.

Measured on the r14 tree: `grep -l 'printed box with no input' forms/*/index.html forms/extra/*/index.html` returns 53 of 53 bundles (it returned 0 when the finding was raised), and `grep -l 'no usable box' ...` returns 0 (it returned 38).
